subject: SLA/support redlines — uptime targets, credit model, and maintenance windows
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SLA/support redlines — attached draft and proposed options

Hi Maria —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the Order Form. Attached is our consolidated redline for the MSA and the Order Form SLA section (redline_MSA_v3.docx and OrderForm-SLA-markup.pdf). Key items we flagged: uptime measurement window, definition of "Availability", service credit caps, and the maintenance blackout / rolling maintenance language.

High-level proposals we think will keep operational risk managed while remaining commercially reasonable:
- Availability measured monthly with a 5‑minute incident exclusion for short network flaps; keep uptime target at 99.9% for Hosted API and 99.5% for Dedicated pools.
- Monthly service credit threshold starting at <99.9% for Hosted, with a 25% cap on credits per month (we call this out to preserve capacity economics).
- Response SLAs (P1/P2) tied to Business Hours with an optional 24x7 for an additional support add-on in the Order Form (we flagged both options).
- Maintenance windows: we propose a rolling window with 48 hours’ notice for non-emergency maintenance and a single 8‑hour blackout per regional week for major upgrades; emergency maintenance allowed with best-effort notice.

Can you confirm whether Acme needs the 24x7 guaranteed response in the base offering (they had mentioned high compliance requirements), or if that’s something we can provide as an upsell? If they need lower credit caps or different uptime bands we can model that against pricing.

I attached a short summary in the doc and highlighted suggested legal wording. If helpful I can jump on a quick 30‑minute sync today at 3pm PT.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
irene.ch@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0117

Attachments: redline_MSA_v3.docx (MS Word redline), OrderForm-SLA-markup.pdf (PDF annotated)

From: Acme Legal <acme-legal@acme.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA/support redlines — attached draft and proposed options

Irene —

Thanks for the file. A few immediate items from our side:
1) Acme is requesting a 99.95% uptime target for the Hosted API (our apps are customer-facing).
2) Service credit pool: legal would like uncapped credits up to 100% of the monthly invoice for sustained outages >72 hours.
3) Response times: for Severity 1 we need a guaranteed 1‑hour response and 4‑hour mitigation for critical incidents in the base contract.
4) Maintenance windows: we cannot accept routine maintenance during our PST business hours (8am–8pm PDT) for the east coast production rollout next quarter; we need a stricter blackout or pre-agreed maintenance calendar.

Can you get internal signoff on the above? If these items require a pricing amendment we need an initial direction: (a) accept and escalate to pricing; or (b) offer a Premium SLA add-on with defined pricing tiers.

—Acme Legal (on behalf of María)
Acme Corporation
acme-legal@acme.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA/support redlines — internal notes

Irene / Lauren —

Quick internal take before we respond to Acme:
- 99.95% Hosted: incremental operational cost is non-trivial; we should only offer 99.95% with dedication to a reserved capacity plan or an explicit Premium SLA fee. Recommend we push back on base 99.9% and present two options (Standard 99.9% included; Premium 99.95% + 20% surcharge / or listed price).
- Uncapped credits: cannot accept. Propose a capped model tied to trailing three‑month invoice average; propose cap = 100% of a single monthly invoice for sustained severe outages >72h but no more than 200% across rolling 3 months. If legal insists on uncapped, escalate to finance.
- Response SLA: 1‑hour response / 4‑hour mitigation is aggressive. We can commit to 1‑hour acknowledge for P1 and a 6‑hour mitigation SLA for base, with optional 4‑hour mitigation on Premium SLA only.
- Maintenance blackout: operationally we can agree to a customer-defined blackout week for the east coast rollout but not a permanent daytime blackout for all customers. Recommend we offer a dedicated calendar and 8‑hour maintenance slot per regional week with an option to purchase additional blackout windows.

Irene — if you can present the two-tier pricing option and call out what has to be Premium we should be in a good negotiating position.

-Jonas
Director, Solutions Ops
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com>
To: Acme Legal <acme-legal@acme.com>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-30T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA/support redlines — proposed path forward

Maria / Acme team —

Thanks for the clear asks — we've reviewed internally and propose the following path forward to keep things moving: 

1) Two-tier SLA approach (keeps procurement flexible):
   - Standard SLA (included): 99.9% Hosted Availability, credit schedule capped at 100% of a single monthly invoice per calendar month, P1 acknowledge within 1 hour / mitigation target 6 hours, maintenance rolling window with 48 hours' notice and one 8‑hour regional maintenance slot per week.
   - Premium SLA (add-on): 99.95% Hosted Availability, credit schedule increase (cap up to 200% over rolling 3 months), P1 mitigation target 4 hours, guaranteed 24x7 response, and ability to request additional blackout weeks for scheduled rollouts (pre-scheduled and agreed in the Order Form). Pricing impact: roughly +20–30% on top of base committed capacity (we will provide a precise amendment).

2) Uncapped credits: we cannot accept fully uncapped credits. If Acme requires uncapped remediation we will need to route to Finance for a bespoke commercial arrangement; please confirm if you want us to open that discussion.

3) Maintenance calendar: we can commit to a pre-agreed maintenance calendar for your east-coast rollout window and exclude that window from routine maintenance; we will not accept permanent daytime blackout across all customers but will provide a dedicated per-account calendar entry in the Order Form for major rollouts.

I attached the annotated Order Form with the proposed Premium/Standard toggles. Next steps: let us know whether Acme prefers Premium SLA as baseline or wants to proceed with Standard and purchase Premium for the rollout. Happy to join a call with María and procurement tomorrow morning if that helps.

Best,
Irene
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
irene.ch@redwood.com
